items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: The interviewee mentions Elvis only in the context of the interviewer's question about the 'rock & roll era' and 'Elvis and all of that' affecting employment. The interviewee responds by discussing their own career moves to Canada and playing jazz standards, without indicating any personal interacti

ctx.x: I think I can say that I was a professional in 1950. That is in jazz music and classical music.
I was just wondering if the rock & roll era, and the British invasion of rock & roll and Elvis and all of that, if it affected your employment. © Fillius Jazz Archive -30-

It did, it did. That’s why we were slick enough to go to Canada. Because Canada was twenty years behind the United States. Exactly twenty years. So when we went to Canada, we were like heroes and they really thought that we were the cat’s meow. And we could play Duke Ellington and we could play Count Basie, and could play, of course we did, we had to do “Blueberry Hill” — Fats Domino, they’d say in Quebec. But by the same time Louis Armstrong had a hit on “Blueberry Hill” also. And although we threw in some of…
